claim: Sox9 mRNA is expressed in the VZ, but not SVZ, of E14.5 mouse neocortex.
source: In the germinal zones of embryonic day (E) 14.5 mouse neocortex, Sox9 mRNA was found to be expressed in the VZ, but not SVZ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, left)
evidence: The claim is supported by FPKM values from published transcriptome datasets (Fietz et al., 2012) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SOX9 mRNA is expressed in the VZ, ISVZ and OSVZ of 13–16 wpc human neocortex.
source: in the 13–16 weeks post conception (wpc) human neocortex, SOX9 mRNA was found to be expressed not only in the VZ, but also in the ISVZ and OSVZ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, right) (Fietz et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by FPKM values from published transcriptome datasets (Fietz et al., 2012) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No significant Sox9/SOX9 mRNA expression is observed in the cortical plate (CP) of mouse and human neocortex.
source: In both species, no significant Sox9/SOX9 mRNA expression was observed in the cortical plate (CP).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of published transcriptome data (Fietz et al., 2012) referenced in the preceding sentences.

claim: Sox9 mRNA is highly expressed in aRG, but not in bRG, bIPs and neurons in E14.5 mouse neocortex.
source: In specific cNPC types isolated from E14.5 mouse neocortex, Sox9 mRNA was highly expressed in aRG, but not in bRG, bIPs and neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, left) (Florio et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by FPKM values from published transcriptome datasets (Florio et al., 2015) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Sox9 mRNA levels in mouse aRG are almost three times higher in the proliferative aRG subpopulation lacking Tis21-GFP expression than in the neurogenic aRG subpopulation exhibiting Tis21-GFP expression.
source: Within mouse aRG, Sox9 mRNA levels were almost three times as high in the proliferative aRG subpopulation that lacks Tis21-GFP expression than in the neurogenic aRG subpopulation that exhibits Tis21-GFP expression.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of published transcriptome data (Florio et al., 2015) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SOX9 mRNA is highly expressed in aRG and also found in bRG in 13 wpc human neocortex.
source: In contrast to mouse, in specific cNPC types isolated from 13 wpc human neocortex, SOX9 mRNA was highly expressed in aRG, but was also found in bRG (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, right) (Florio et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by FPKM values from published transcriptome datasets (Florio et al., 2015) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Sox9 protein is restricted to the VZ in E14.5 mouse neocortex.
source: Consistent with the Sox9 mRNA data (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1), the Sox9 protein was restricted to the VZ in E14.5 mouse neocortex (Figure 1A,G)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A and 1G.

claim: Sox9 protein is abundantly expressed in the VZ, ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret neocortex.
source: the Sox9 protein was restricted to the VZ in E14.5 mouse neocortex (Figure 1A,G), but was abundantly expressed in the VZ, ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret (a typical developmental stage for the analysis of cNPCs in the context of cortical neurogenesis [Kalebic et al., 2018]) and 15 wpc human neocortex (Figure 1B,C,H,I)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B and 1H, and references a citation (Kalebic et al., 2018) for the developmental stage.

claim: Sox9 protein is abundantly expressed in the VZ, ISVZ and OSVZ of 15 wpc human neocortex.
source: the Sox9 protein was restricted to the VZ in E14.5 mouse neocortex (Figure 1A,G), but was abundantly expressed in the VZ, ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret (a typical developmental stage for the analysis of cNPCs in the context of cortical neurogenesis [Kalebic et al., 2018]) and 15 wpc human neocortex (Figure 1B,C,H,I)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C and 1I.

claim: Sox9 protein shows a nuclear localization at the subcellular level.
source: At the subcellular level, the Sox9 protein showed a nuclear localization.
evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence observations described in the preceding paragraph and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Sox9 protein is expressed in BPs of ferret and human, but not mouse, neocortex.
source: These data suggested that the Sox9 protein is expressed in BPs of ferret and human, but not mouse, neocortex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the immunofluorescence data showing Sox9 expression patterns in the VZ and SVZ of mouse, ferret, and human neocortex.

claim: Virtually all Sox9-expressing cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret neocortex co-express Sox2.
source: Double immunofluorescence showed that virtually all Sox9-expressing cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex co-expressed Sox2, implying that these cells were proliferative BPs, and that these cells comprised about half of the Sox2-positive BPs (Figure 1B,C,E,F)
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B, 1C, 1E, and 1F.

claim: Virtually all Sox9-expressing cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of 15 wpc human neocortex co-express Sox2.
source: Double immunofluorescence showed that virtually all Sox9-expressing cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex co-expressed Sox2, implying that these cells were proliferative BPs, and that these cells comprised about half of the Sox2-positive BPs (Figure 1B,C,E,F)
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B, 1C, 1E, and 1F.

claim: Sox9 and Sox2 double-positive cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of ferret and human neocortex are proliferative BPs.
source: Double immunofluorescence showed that virtually all Sox9-expressing cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex co-expressed Sox2, implying that these cells were proliferative BPs
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the co-expression of Sox9 and Sox2, where Sox2 is known to be characteristic of proliferative BPs.

claim: Sox9 and Sox2 double-positive cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of ferret and human neocortex comprise about half of the Sox2-positive BPs.
source: Double immunofluorescence showed that virtually all Sox9-expressing cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex co-expressed Sox2, implying that these cells were proliferative BPs, and that these cells comprised about half of the Sox2-positive BPs (Figure 1B,C,E,F)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of double immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E and 1F.

claim: 70–80% of Sox2-positive cells in the VZ of developing mouse, ferret and human neocortex also express Sox9.
source: Of note, regarding the VZ of developing mouse, ferret and human neocortex, while nearly all cells were Sox2-positive, 70–80% of these also expressed Sox9 (Figure 1A–F)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of double immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A-F.

claim: Sox2-positive cells in the VZ that also express Sox9 are cNPCs.
source: Of note, regarding the VZ of developing mouse, ferret and human neocortex, while nearly all cells were Sox2-positive, 70–80% of these also expressed Sox9 (Figure 1A–F), again in line with these cells being cNPCs.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the known identity of Sox2-positive cells in the VZ as cNPCs.

claim: Virtually none of the Sox9-positive cells express Tbr2 in the germinal zones of E14.5 mouse, E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex.
source: Double immunofluorescence of the E14.5 mouse, E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex for Sox9 and Tbr2 revealed that in all germinal zones, virtually none of the Sox9-positive cells expressed Tbr2, indicative of a mutually exclusive expression pattern (Figure 1G–L)
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G-L.

claim: Sox9 and Tbr2 exhibit a mutually exclusive expression pattern in the germinal zones of E14.5 mouse, E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex.
source: Double immunofluorescence of the E14.5 mouse, E40 ferret and 15 wpc human neocortex for Sox9 and Tbr2 revealed that in all germinal zones, virtually none of the Sox9-positive cells expressed Tbr2, indicative of a mutually exclusive expression pattern (Figure 1G–L)
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G-L.

claim: Sox9 and Sox2 double-positive cells in the VZ of mouse, ferret and human neocortex are aRG.
source: Regarding the VZ, these data imply that the Sox9 and Sox2 double-positive cells observed in the three species (Figure 1D–F) are aRG
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the mutually exclusive expression of Sox9 and Tbr2, and the known identity of Sox2-positive cells in the VZ.

claim: Sox9-negative but Sox2-positive cells in the VZ of mouse, ferret and human neocortex are newborn BPs, notably newborn bIPs.
source: whereas the Sox9-negative but Sox2-positive cells (Figure 1D–F) are newborn BPs, notably newborn bIPs
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the mutually exclusive expression of Sox9 and Tbr2, and the known identity of Tbr2-positive cells as newborn bIPs.

claim: Sox9 and Sox2 double-positive cells in the SVZ of ferret and human neocortex are proliferative BPs, likely bRG, rather than neurogenic bIPs.
source: Regarding the SVZ, these data suggest that the Sox9 and Sox2 double-positive cells observed in ferret and human are proliferative BPs, likely bRG, rather than neurogenic bIPs.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the mutually exclusive expression of Sox9 and Tbr2, and the known characteristics of different BP types.

claim: Sox9 expression is down-regulated upon BPs becoming committed to neurogenesis.
source: The latter conclusion in turn implies that Sox9 expression is down-regulated upon BPs becoming committed to neurogenesis.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the mutually exclusive expression of Sox9 and Tbr2, where Tbr2 is a marker of neurogenic commitment.

claim: The vast majority of Sox9-positive cells in the three germinal zones of P2 and P3 ferret neocortex are cycling.
source: We first performed immunofluorescence for the cell cycle marker PCNA on postnatal day (P) two and P3 ferret neocortex and found that the vast majority of the Sox9-positive cells in the three germinal zones were cycling (Figure 2A,A', B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for PCNA shown in Figure 2A, 2A', and 2B.

claim: The vast majority of Sox9-positive progeny in the VZ and OSVZ of P2/P3 ferret neocortex can re-enter the next cell cycle.
source: We observed that the vast majority of the Sox9-positive progeny in the VZ and OSVZ can re-enter the next cell cycle at P2/P3 (Figure 2C), suggesting that the daughter cells of the EdU-labeled cNPCs maintained proliferative capacity.
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU pulse-chase and PCNA immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The daughter cells of EdU-labeled Sox9-positive cNPCs in ferret neocortex maintain proliferative capacity.
source: We observed that the vast majority of the Sox9-positive progeny in the VZ and OSVZ can re-enter the next cell cycle at P2/P3 (Figure 2C), suggesting that the daughter cells of the EdU-labeled cNPCs maintained proliferative capacity.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the EdU pulse-chase experiment showing cell cycle re-entry.

claim: Sox9-expressing BPs in the OSVZ of developing ferret neocortex exhibit a high proliferative capacity.
source: We conclude that in the developing ferret neocortex, the Sox9-expressing BPs in the OSVZ, like the Sox9-expressing aRG in the VZ, exhibit a high proliferative capacity.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the cell cycle re-entry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Essentially all mitotic aRG in the VZ of 13 wpc human neocortex are Sox9-positive.
source: In 13 wpc human neocortex, essentially all mitotic aRG in the VZ and the overwhelming majority of the mitotic BPs in the SVZ were Sox9-positive (Figure 2E)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Sox9 and phospho-vimentin shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The overwhelming majority of mitotic BPs in the SVZ of 13 wpc human neocortex are Sox9-positive.
source: In 13 wpc human neocortex, essentially all mitotic aRG in the VZ and the overwhelming majority of the mitotic BPs in the SVZ were Sox9-positive (Figure 2E)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Sox9 and phospho-vimentin shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Mitotic BPs in the SVZ of 13 wpc human neocortex exhibit a basal process and are bRG.
source: Moreover, in line with previous observations (Fietz et al., 2010), the mitotic BPs exhibited a basal process and thus were bRG (Figure 2F)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2F and is consistent with previous observations (Fietz et al., 2010).

claim: All mitotic bRG in the SVZ of 13 wpc human neocortex express Sox9.
source: Importantly, all of the latter expressed Sox9, indicating that bRG in the fetal human neocortex are Sox9-positive (Figure 2G)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: bRG in the fetal human neocortex are Sox9-positive.
source: Importantly, all of the latter expressed Sox9, indicating that bRG in the fetal human neocortex are Sox9-positive (Figure 2G)
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the immunofluorescence data showing Sox9 expression in mitotic bRG.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of Sox9 in embryonic ferret neocortex results in a strong reduction of the Sox9 protein in all germinal zones four days after in utero electroporation.
source: We examined the efficiency of the knockout (KO) four days after in utero electroporation, at E37, and detected a strong reduction of the Sox9 protein in all germinal zones of the ferret neocortex (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,B', C)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, B', and C.

claim: Sox9 KO in embryonic ferret neocortex results in a striking reduction in the proportion of PCNA+ cells throughout the SVZ, particularly in the OSVZ (50% reduction).
source: We examined the effects of Sox9 KO on BP proliferation by immunofluorescence for PCNA, a marker of cycling cells (Figure 3A), and found a striking reduction in proportion of PCNA+ cells throughout the SVZ, and particularly in the OSVZ (50% reduction) (Figure 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for PCNA shown in Figure 3A and quantification in Figure 3B.

claim: Sox9 KO in embryonic ferret neocortex results in a decrease in mitoses throughout the ferret germinal zones.
source: Immunofluorescence of pVim (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), a marker of mitotic cells, corroborated these data, showing a decrease in mitoses throughout the ferret germinal zones (Figure 3C)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for pVim shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and quantification in Figure 3C.

claim: Sox9 KO in embryonic ferret neocortex results in a decrease in the proportion of Sox2-positive cells with radial orientation and radial processes (bRG-like cells) in the total SVZ and particularly in the OSVZ.
source: Finally, to examine if these effects pertained also to bRG, the subset of BPs that is thought to be instrumental for the evolutionary expansion of the neocortex, we focused on Sox2-positive cells in the SVZ that exhibited a radial orientation of the nucleus and the presence of radial processes (Kalebic et al., 2018) (basal and/or apical, see Figure 3—figure supplement 2, inset for examples of a bRG and a multipolar BP). We found a decrease in the proportion of these cells in the total SVZ, and in particular in the OSVZ, upon Sox9 KO (Figure 3E)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and quantification in Figure 3E, and references a citation (Kalebic et al., 2018) for the morphological criteria.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KO of Sox9 in embryonic ferret neocortex results in a decrease of BP proliferation.
source: Taken together, our data show that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KO of Sox9 in embryonic ferret neocortex results in a decrease of BP proliferation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the PCNA, pVim, and Sox2 immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The decrease in BP proliferation upon Sox9 KO in embryonic ferret neocortex pertains to both multipolar BPs and bRG.
source: Importantly, this decrease pertains to both types of BPs (multipolar BPs and bRG).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the Sox2 immunofluorescence data showing effects on both total Sox2+ BPs and bRG-like cells.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs doubles the proportion of cycling cells (Ki67+) in the SVZ and IZ at E15.5.
source: Indeed, conditional Sox9 expression doubled the proportion of cells in the SVZ and intermediate zone (IZ) derived from the targeted cells (as revealed by RFP expression) that were cycling and hence were BPs, both upon analysis at E15.5 (Figure 4C,C', D,D', G) and at E14.5 (Figure 4H)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Ki67 shown in Figure 4C, C', D, D' and quantification in Figure 4G.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs doubles the proportion of cycling cells (Ki67+) in the SVZ and IZ at E14.5.
source: Indeed, conditional Sox9 expression doubled the proportion of cells in the SVZ and intermediate zone (IZ) derived from the targeted cells (as revealed by RFP expression) that were cycling and hence were BPs, both upon analysis at E15.5 (Figure 4C,C', D,D', G) and at E14.5 (Figure 4H)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Ki67 and quantification in Figure 4H.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs markedly increases the proportion of targeted cell-derived (RFP+) BPs that undergo mitosis.
source: To corroborate the effect of conditional Sox9 expression on mouse BP proliferation, we analyzed the abundance of basal mitoses by performing immunofluorescence for phospho-histone H3 one day after electroporation at E13.5 (Figure 4E,F,F'). Conditional Sox9 expression markedly increased the proportion of the targeted cell-derived (RFP+) BPs that underwent mitosis (Figure 4I)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for phospho-histone H3 shown in Figure 4E, F, F' and quantification in Figure 4I.

claim: The Sox9-induced increase in the proliferation of mouse BPs pertains primarily to bIPs.
source: Immunofluorescence for phospho-vimentin at E15.5 did not provide evidence that a noteworthy fraction of the targeted cell-derived (RFP+) mitotic BPs observed upon conditional Sox9 expression exhibited a prominent radial process (Figure 4J). This suggested that the Sox9-induced increase in the proliferation of mouse BPs pertained primarily to bIPs.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the lack of prominent radial processes in RFP+ mitotic BPs, as shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs doubles the proportion of targeted cell-derived (RFP+) mitotic (pVim+) BPs that are Pax6-negative (bIPs).
source: This revealed that conditional Sox9 expression doubled the proportion of the targeted cell-derived (RFP+) mitotic (pVim+) BPs that were Pax6-negative, that is bIPs (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for RFP, pVim, and Pax6 shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A, A' and quantification in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs significantly increases the proportion of targeted cell-derived (RFP+), EdU-containing cells in the SVZ plus IZ that are Ki67+ and hence cycling BPs.
source: This revealed that conditional Sox9 expression significantly increased the proportion of targeted cell-derived (RFP+), EdU-containing cells in the SVZ plus IZ that were Ki67+ and hence were cycling BPs (Figure 4M)
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU pulse-chase and Ki67 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4K, K', L, L' and quantification in Figure 4M.

claim: The progeny of BPs exhibit an increased ability to re-enter the cell cycle upon conditional Sox9 expression.
source: These data are consistent with the progeny of BPs exhibiting an increased ability to re-enter the cell cycle, that is to remain being BPs (as opposed to becoming postmitotic neurons).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the EdU pulse-chase and Ki67 immunofluorescence data showing increased cell cycle re-entry.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs decreases the abundance of Tbr2-positive cells at E15.5, especially in the SVZ.
source: Tbr2 immunofluorescence of mouse neocortex electroporated at E13.5 revealed that conditional Sox9 expression decreased the abundance of Tbr2-positive cells at E15.5 (Figure 5A,B), especially in the SVZ (Figure 5A', B')
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Tbr2 shown in Figure 5A, A', B, B'.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs reduces the proportion of targeted cell-derived (RFP+) BPs in the SVZ that express Tbr2 to half.
source: Specifically, conditional Sox9 expression reduced the proportion of targeted cell-derived (RFP+) BPs in the SVZ that expressed Tbr2 to half (Figure 5C)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs may alter their identity and fate, possibly reducing their commitment to neurogenesis.
source: These findings provided a first indication that conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs may alter their identity and fate, possibly reducing their commitment to neurogenesis.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduction in Tbr2 expression upon conditional Sox9 expression.

claim: Less than one fifth of Sox9-positive cells in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40/P1 ferret neocortex are Olig2-positive.
source: Double immunofluorescence for Sox9 and Olig2 of E40 ferret neocortex revealed scattered double-positive cells in the ferret ISVZ and OSVZ (see Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and A'), which upon quantification amounted to less than one fifth of the Sox9-positive cells in these germinal zones at E40/P1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Sox9 and Olig2 shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, A' and quantification in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Essentially all Sox9-positive cells in the E40/P1 ISVZ and OSVZ of ferret neocortex are Sox2-positive and hence BPs.
source: Given that essentially all Sox9-positive cells in the E40/P1 ISVZ and OSVZ of ferret neocortex are Sox2-positive (Figure 1E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,A', C) and hence BPs, we conclude that only a minority of these progenitors are committed to gliogenesis at the developmental stages studied.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, A', C.

claim: Only a minority of Sox9-positive BPs in the ISVZ and OSVZ of E40/P1 ferret neocortex are committed to gliogenesis.
source: Given that essentially all Sox9-positive cells in the E40/P1 ISVZ and OSVZ of ferret neocortex are Sox2-positive (Figure 1E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,A', C) and hence BPs, we conclude that only a minority of these progenitors are committed to gliogenesis at the developmental stages studied.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the quantification of Sox9 and Olig2 double-positive cells.

claim: No Olig2 immunoreactivity is detected in the E15.5 mouse neocortical wall upon control electroporation at E13.5.
source: We next examined whether mouse BPs conditionally expressing Sox9 include gliogenic precursor cells. No Olig2 immunoreactivity was detected in the E15.5 neocortical wall by immunofluorescence upon control electroporation at E13.5 (Figure 5D), in line with the onset of neocortical gliogenesis in mouse occurring later, that is around E18.5 (Miller and Gauthier, 2007)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5D and is consistent with the known timing of gliogenesis onset (Miller and Gauthier, 2007).

claim: Upon conditional Sox9 expression for two days, many Olig2-positive cells are observed in the SVZ and IZ of E15.5 mouse neocortex.
source: Remarkably, however, upon conditional Sox9 expression for two days, many Olig2-positive cells were observed in the SVZ and IZ (Figure 5E,E')
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Olig2 shown in Figure 5E, E'.

claim: 22% of targeted cell-derived (RFP+) BPs in the mouse E15.5 SVZ and IZ have adopted a gliogenic identity upon conditional Sox9 expression.
source: Quantification of Olig2 and RFP double-positive cells revealed that 22% of the targeted cell-derived (RFP+) BPs in the mouse E15.5 SVZ and IZ had adopted a gliogenic identity (Figure 5F)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Relative Sox9 expression is highest in the High RFP population from Sox9-electroporated neocortex and much lower in the Low RFP population from the same sample.
source: We first examined Sox9 mRNA levels by quantitative PCR on these sorted cell populations and observed that relative Sox9 expression was highest in the High RFP population from Sox9-electroporated neocortex and was much lower in the Low RFP population from the same sample (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Relative expression of Tbr2 mRNA is almost completely repressed in the High RFP population of Sox9-electroporated neocortex.
source: We next analyzed mRNA levels for Tbr2 and Olig2 and found that relative expression of Tbr2 mRNA was almost completely repressed (Figure 5H) and relative expression of Olig2 mRNA was specifically induced (Figure 5I) in the High RFP population of Sox9-electroporated neocortex
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Relative expression of Olig2 mRNA is specifically induced in the High RFP population of Sox9-electroporated neocortex.
source: We next analyzed mRNA levels for Tbr2 and Olig2 and found that relative expression of Tbr2 mRNA was almost completely repressed (Figure 5H) and relative expression of Olig2 mRNA was specifically induced (Figure 5I) in the High RFP population of Sox9-electroporated neocortex
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: High Sox9 levels in mouse BPs induce a switch in their cell fate to gliogenesis by inducing Olig2 mRNA and repressing Tbr2 mRNA expression.
source: We conclude that high Sox9 levels in mouse BPs induce a switch in their cell fate to gliogenesis by inducing Olig2 mRNA and repressing Tbr2 mRNA expression.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the qPCR data showing dose-dependent effects of Sox9 on Tbr2 and Olig2 expression.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs increases the percentage of RFP+ cells in the SVZ that are Sox2-positive at E14.5.
source: Quantification of the percentage of the RFP+ cells in the SVZ that were Sox2-positive revealed an increase upon Sox9 expression (Figure 5L)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Sox2 shown in Figure 5J, K and quantification in Figure 5L.

claim: Upon conditional Sox9 expression at E13.5, 10–15% of the RFP+ cells in the SVZ are still positive for Tbr2 at E15.5.
source: Given that upon conditional Sox9 expression at E13.5, 10–15% of the RFP+ cells in the SVZ are still positive for Tbr2 at E15.5 (Figure 5C), this observation suggests that the increased number of BPs consist of a mix of neurogenic and gliogenic progenitors.
evidence: The claim is based on quantification data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The increased number of BPs upon conditional Sox9 expression consists of a mix of neurogenic and gliogenic progenitors.
source: Given that upon conditional Sox9 expression at E13.5, 10–15% of the RFP+ cells in the SVZ are still positive for Tbr2 at E15.5 (Figure 5C), this observation suggests that the increased number of BPs consist of a mix of neurogenic and gliogenic progenitors.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the presence of both Tbr2+ and Sox2+ cells among RFP+ BPs.

claim: Differential gene expression analysis comparing conditionally Sox9 expressing vs control High RFP cells yielded 749 downregulated and 870 upregulated protein-encoding genes (q < 0.01).
source: In order to identify the genes that were affected by conditional Sox9 expression, we performed differential gene expression (DGE) analysis by comparing the expression levels of only protein-encoding genes in conditionally Sox9 expressing vs control High RFP cells. This yielded 749 downregulated and 870 upregulated protein-encoding genes upon Sox9 expression (q < 0.01) (Figure 6B, Supplementary file 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: GO term enrichment analysis of the 870 genes upregulated in Sox9-expressing cells revealed that the highest enrichment scores most frequently included genes related to the ECM.
source: To gain insight into the cell biological processes affected by conditional Sox9 expression, we examined the 870 genes upregulated in Sox9-expressing cells by gene ontology (GO) term enrichment analysis for biological process (Figure 6C) and cellular component (Figure 6D). This analysis revealed that the highest enrichment scores most frequently included genes related to the ECM (Figure 6C and D)
evidence: The claim is supported by GO term enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6C and 6D.

claim: KEGG pathway analysis of the 870 genes upregulated in Sox9-expressing cells yielded the highest enrichment scores for ECM production, organization and degradation.
source: Similarly, KEGG pathway analysis using the same gene set as input yielded the highest enrichment scores for ECM production, organization and degradation (Figure 6E)
evidence: The claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: 203 of the 870 genes upregulated in Sox9-expressing cells are related to the ECM.
source: GO term enrichment and KEGG pathway analyses indicated that 203 of the 870 genes upregulated in Sox9-expressing cells were related to the ECM (Figure 6C–E, Supplementary file 3)
evidence: The claim is supported by GO term enrichment and KEGG pathway analyses shown in Figure 6C-E and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression induces the expression of gliogenic genes such as Olig2 and S100b.
source: In addition to the upregulation of expression of ECM components, conditional Sox9 expression induced the expression of gliogenic genes such as Olig2 and S100b (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and B), corroborating the effect of conditional Sox9 expression on gliogenesis observed by immunohistochemistry (Figure 5E and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and B, and is consistent with immunohistochemistry data in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs results in significant increases in the numbers of Ki67-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ.
source: Quantification per unit area of the numbers of Ki67-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ (Figure 7D), of PH3-positive and RFP-negative abventricular mitoses (Figure 7E), and of Sox2-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ (Figure 7F) revealed significant increases for all three cell populations in conditionally Sox9-expressing neocortex
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs results in significant increases in the numbers of PH3-positive and RFP-negative abventricular mitoses.
source: Quantification per unit area of the numbers of Ki67-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ (Figure 7D), of PH3-positive and RFP-negative abventricular mitoses (Figure 7E), and of Sox2-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ (Figure 7F) revealed significant increases for all three cell populations in conditionally Sox9-expressing neocortex
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs results in significant increases in the numbers of Sox2-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ.
source: Quantification per unit area of the numbers of Ki67-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ (Figure 7D), of PH3-positive and RFP-negative abventricular mitoses (Figure 7E), and of Sox2-positive and RFP-negative nuclei in SVZ+IZ (Figure 7F) revealed significant increases for all three cell populations in conditionally Sox9-expressing neocortex
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs results in a cell non-autonomous stimulation of BP proliferation.
source: These findings indicate that conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs not only increases their proliferation cell-autonomously (see Figure 4), but also results in a cell non-autonomous stimulation of BP proliferation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the increased proliferation of RFP-negative BPs upon conditional Sox9 expression.

claim: The percentage of NeuN-positive nuclei in the CP is significantly increased upon conditional Sox9 expression at E17.5.
source: Specifically, we performed immunofluorescence for NeuN at E17.5 of mouse neocortex electroporated at E13.5 (Figure 7G and H), and found that the percentage of NeuN-positive nuclei in the CP was significantly increased upon conditional Sox9 expression (Figure 7I)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for NeuN shown in Figure 7G, H and quantification in Figure 7I.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in BPs results in a significant increase in the percentage of nuclei in the CP that are RFP-negative and NeuN-positive.
source: Further examination of the NeuN-positive nuclei in the CP showed that conditional Sox9 expression in BPs resulted in a significant increase in the percentage of nuclei that were RFP-negative and NeuN-positive (Figure 7K)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7K.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs results in increased neuron production from BPs whose proliferation was stimulated in a cell non-autonomous manner.
source: Taken together, we conclude that conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs results in increased neuron production from BPs whose proliferation was stimulated in a cell non-autonomous manner.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the increased NeuN-positive, RFP-negative neurons in the CP.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in BPs results in a significant, more than two-fold increase in the number of EdU+ Satb2+ RFP- cells in the CP at E17.5.
source: On the one hand, conditional Sox9 expression in BPs resulted in a significant, more than two-fold increase in the number EdU-containing (EdU+) cells in the CP that were Satb2-positive and RFP-negative, that is progeny derived from of non-electroporated cells (Figure 7O)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Satb2 and EdU shown in Figure 7L, M and quantification in Figure 7O.

claim: The proportion of EdU+ RFP+ cells that are Tbr1+ is massively decreased upon conditional Sox9 expression in BPs at E17.5.
source: In contrast, the proportion of EdU-containing (EdU+) RFP-positive (RFP+) cells that were Tbr1-positive (Tbr1+) was found to be massively decreased upon conditional Sox9 expression in BPs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Tbr1 and EdU shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B and quantification in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Upon conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs, the production of upper-layer neurons is increased and this increase involves the non-targeted BPs whose proliferation is stimulated in a cell non-autonomous manner.
source: We conclude that upon conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs the production of upper-layer neurons is increased and that this increase involves the non-targeted BPs whose proliferation is stimulated in a cell non-autonomous manner.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the increased Satb2+ RFP- neurons and decreased Tbr1+ RFP+ neurons.

claim: Upon conditional Sox9 expression in BPs, the relative distribution of RFP+ cells in the CP is shifted towards the upper layers, with a significant decrease in the percentage of RFP+ cells in the lower layers (bin 2) and an increase in the upper layers (bin 7) at E18.5.
source: Quantification of the percentage of RFP+ cells in each bin showed that upon conditional Sox9 expression in BPs, the relative distribution of the RFP+ cells was shifted towards the upper layers of the CP, with a significant decrease in the percentage of RFP+ cells in the lower layers of the CP (specifically bin number 2, Figure 8B) and an increase in the percentage of RFP+ cells in the upper layers of the CP (specifically bin number 7, Figure 8B)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of RFP+ cell distribution shown in Figure 8A and 8B.

claim: The proportion of all RFP+ cells in the CP that are Tbr1+ at E18.5 is significantly decreased upon conditional Sox9 expression.
source: Consistent with these data and with the observed decrease in the proportion of EdU-containing RFP-positive cells that were Tbr1-positive at E17.5 upon conditional Sox9 expression (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), the proportion of all RFP+ cells in the CP that were Tbr1+ at E18.5 was significantly decreased upon conditional Sox9 expression (Figure 8C,C', D,D' and G)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Tbr1 shown in Figure 8C, C', D, D' and quantification in Figure 8G.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in BPs results in a significant increase in the abundance of nuclei in the CP that are RFP-negative and Satb2-positive at E18.5.
source: Further analysis of the Satb2-positive nuclei in the CP showed that conditional Sox9 expression in BPs resulted in a significant increase in the abundance (i) of nuclei that were RFP-negative and Satb2-positive (Figure 8I) and (ii) of the total Satb2-positive nuclei in the CP (Figure 8J)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in BPs results in a significant increase in the total abundance of Satb2-positive nuclei in the CP at E18.5.
source: Further analysis of the Satb2-positive nuclei in the CP showed that conditional Sox9 expression in BPs resulted in a significant increase in the abundance (i) of nuclei that were RFP-negative and Satb2-positive (Figure 8I) and (ii) of the total Satb2-positive nuclei in the CP (Figure 8J)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8J.

claim: The increase in Satb2-positive neurons upon conditional Sox9 expression in BPs pertains mostly to progeny derived from non-electroporated cells.
source: These findings corroborate the notion that the increase in Satb2-positive neurons upon conditional Sox9 expression in BPs pertains mostly to progeny derived from non-electroporated cells.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the increased Satb2+ RFP- neurons in the CP.

claim: Laminin α2 mRNA shows a ≈two-fold increase upon conditional Sox9 expression.
source: Specifically, although the laminin α2 mRNA – because of its low FPKM values – was not included in our analysis of the protein-encoding genes upregulated upon conditional Sox9 expression, it did show a ≈two-fold increase upon conditional Sox9 expression (Figure 9A)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Lamb1 and Lamc1 mRNAs exhibit expression levels in both the control condition and upon conditional Sox9 expression in the mouse BP lineage that are consistent with the occurrence of laminin 211 in the embryonic mouse neocortex under these conditions.
source: In addition, the mRNAs for the beta and gamma chains required to form a functional laminin 211 heterotrimer, Lamb1 and Lamc1, were found to exhibit expression levels in both the control condition and upon conditional Sox nine expression in the mouse BP lineage that were consistent with the occurrence of laminin 211 in the embryonic mouse neocortex under these conditions (Figure 9B,C)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 9B and 9C.

claim: Collagen 4α1 mRNA shows a > 3 fold increase upon conditional Sox9 expression.
source: Similar considerations pertained to the collagen 4α1 mRNA, one of the 870 genes upregulated upon conditional Sox nine expression (Supplementary file 1), which showed a > 3 fold increase in this condition (Figure 9D)
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 9D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Laminin 211, but not collagen IV, causes a significant increase in the proportion of cycling cells (Ki67+) specifically in the SVZ, but not VZ, of E14.5 mouse neocortical organotypic slice cultures.
source: Following the treatment of organotypic slices of E14.5 wildtype mouse neocortex without or with recombinant collagen IV or laminin 211, our analysis of cell proliferation by immunofluorescence for Ki67 and phosphohistone H3 (Figure 9E,E') revealed that laminin 211, but not collagen IV, caused a significant increase in the proportion of cycling cells (Ki67+) specifically in the SVZ, but not VZ (Figure 9F)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for Ki67 shown in Figure 9E, E' and quantification in Figure 9F.

claim: The number of basal mitoses (PH3+) per unit area is strikingly increased by laminin 211, but not by collagen IV, in E14.5 mouse neocortical organotypic slice cultures.
source: In addition, the number of basal mitoses (PH3+) per unit area was strikingly increased by laminin 211, but not by collagen IV, whereas the number of apical mitoses was largely unaffected by either ECM component (Figure 9G)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data for PH3 shown in Figure 9E, E'' and quantification in Figure 9G.

claim: The number of apical mitoses is largely unaffected by either collagen IV or laminin 211 in E14.5 mouse neocortical organotypic slice cultures.
source: In addition, the number of basal mitoses (PH3+) per unit area was strikingly increased by laminin 211, but not by collagen IV, whereas the number of apical mitoses was largely unaffected by either ECM component (Figure 9G)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 9G.

claim: Conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs increases the expression of specific ECM components, notably laminins, which potentially promote BP proliferation in an autocrine (RFP-positive BPs, cell autonomous) and paracrine (RFP-negative BPs, cell non-autonomous) manner.
source: These findings provide strong support for the concept that conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs increases the expression of specific ECM components, notably laminins, which potentially promote BP proliferation in an autocrine (RFP-positive BPs, cell autonomous) and paracrine (RFP-negative BPs, cell non-autonomous) manner.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the laminin 211 organotypic slice culture experiments and the RNA-seq data showing increased ECM component expression.

claim: Sox9 is a major inducer of ECM components.
source: Corroborating our considerations at the start of this study, that is that Sox9 – when expressed in the SVZ – could be a promising candidate to drive the expression of ECM components in BPs, our transcriptome analysis upon conditional Sox9 expression in mouse BPs revealed that, indeed, the 870 genes upregulated in Sox9-expressing BPs were predominantly related to the ECM by GO term enrichment analysis.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the GO term enrichment analysis of genes upregulated upon conditional Sox9 expression.

claim: The cell non-autonomous stimulation of BP proliferation by Sox9 is likely due to ECM components that have been secreted from Sox9-expressing BPs and then act on neighboring BPs that themselves have not been targeted to express Sox9.
source: It therefore seems likely that the cell non-autonomous stimulation of mouse BP proliferation upon conditional Sox9 expression is due to ECM components that have been secreted from Sox9-expressing BPs and then act on neighboring BPs that themselves have not been targeted to express Sox9.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the known role of ECM components in stimulating cNPC proliferation and the observed cell non-autonomous effects.

claim: Sox9 promotes BP proliferation cell-autonomously and non-autonomously.
source: Sox9 promotes BP proliferation cell-autonomously and non-autonomously
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data showing both direct and indirect effects of Sox9 on BP proliferation.

claim: Sox9 increases production of upper-layer neurons.
source: Sox9 increases production of upper-layer neurons
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data showing increased Satb2+ neurons upon conditional Sox9 expression.

claim: Sox9 switches BPs to gliogenesis.
source: Sox9 switches BPs to gliogenesis
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data showing induction of Olig2 expression upon conditional Sox9 expression.

claim: An increase in upper-layer neuron production is considered to be one of the hallmarks of neocortical expansion.
source: An increase in upper-layer neuron production is considered to be one of the hallmarks of neocortical expansion (Hutsler et al., 2005; Molnár et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge from cited references (Hutsler et al., 2005; Molnár et al., 2006).

claim: Sox9 has been reported to be expressed simultaneously by mature astrocytes and neurogenic SVZ progenitors in the adult mouse brain.
source: In the adult mouse brain, Sox9 has been reported to be expressed simultaneously by mature astrocytes and neurogenic SVZ progenitors (Cheng et al., 2009; Martini et al., 2013; Nagao et al., 2014; Nait-Oumesmar et al., 2008; Sun et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is based on previous studies cited in the text (Cheng et al., 2009; Martini et al., 2013; Nagao et al., 2014; Nait-Oumesmar et al., 2008; Sun et al., 2017).

claim: Sox9-expressing aRG in the embryonic mouse neocortex are capable of generating neurons for all layers.
source: In the embryonic mouse neocortex, Sox9-expressing aRG have been shown to be capable of generating neurons for all layers (Kaplan et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Kaplan et al., 2017).

claim: Neocortical expansion is characterized not only by an increase in neurogenesis, but also in gliogenesis.
source: Neocortical expansion is characterized not only by an increase in neurogenesis, but also in gliogenesis (Rash et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Rash et al., 2019).

claim: Expression of the human-specific pro-proliferative gene ARHGAP11B leads to an increase in both upper-layer neurons and glia.
source: which might be particularly important in the context of human brain evolution, as recent findings show that expression of the human-specific pro-proliferative gene ARHGAP11B leads to an increase in both upper-layer neurons and glia (Kalebic et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Kalebic et al., 2018).

claim: Sox9 acting in the SVZ shows many of the hallmarks expected for a transcription factor contributing to promote neocortical expansion.
source: Hence, when collectively considering its effects on transcription, BP proliferation and fate, and neuron production, Sox9 acting in the SVZ shows many of the hallmarks expected for a transcription factor contributing to promote neocortical expansion.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the collective experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: The proliferative capacity and pool size of cortical neural progenitor cells (cNPCs) is regarded as a key parameter underlying neocortical expansion.
source: At the cellular level, the proliferative capacity and pool size of cortical neural progenitor cells (cNPCs) is regarded as a key parameter underlying neocortical expansion (Borrell and Reillo, 2012; Dehay et al., 2015; Fernández et al., 2016; Fietz and Huttner, 2011; Fish et al., 2008; Florio and Huttner, 2014; Kriegstein et al., 2006; Lui et al., 2011; Martynoga et al., 2012; Miller et al., 2019; Mitchell and Silver, 2018; Molnár et al., 2019; Namba and Huttner, 2017; Rakic, 2009; Silbereis et al., 2016; Uzquiano et al., 2018; Velasco et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge from multiple cited references.

claim: Neocortical expansion is thought to be linked to an increase in the proliferative capacity of BPs, resulting in their increased pool size and a thickening of the SVZ.
source: Accordingly, neocortical expansion is thought to be linked to an increase in the proliferative capacity of BPs, resulting in their increased pool size and a thickening of the SVZ (Borrell and Reillo, 2012; Dehay et al., 2015; Fernández et al., 2016; Fietz and Huttner, 2011; Florio and Huttner, 2014; Kriegstein et al., 2006; Lui et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge from multiple cited references.

claim: In mammals lacking neocortical expansion, such as mouse, BPs exhibit only low proliferative capacity, typically dividing only once to generate two post-mitotic neurons, and their pool size is relatively small and the SVZ comparably thin.
source: Thus, in mammals lacking neocortical expansion, such as mouse, BPs exhibit only low proliferative capacity, typically dividing only once to generate two post-mitotic neurons, and their pool size is relatively small and the SVZ comparably thin (Arai et al., 2011; Florio and Huttner, 2014; Haubensak et al., 2004; Miyata et al., 2004; Noctor et al., 2004)
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge from multiple cited references.

claim: In mammals showing neocortical expansion, notably human, BPs exhibit high proliferative capacity, resulting in an increased pool size and a thick SVZ.
source: In contrast, in mammals showing neocortical expansion, notably human, BPs exhibit high proliferative capacity, resulting in an increased pool size and a thick SVZ (Betizeau et al., 2013; Fernández et al., 2016; Fietz et al., 2010; Florio and Huttner, 2014; Hansen et al., 2010; Pilz et al., 2013; Reillo et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge from multiple cited references.

claim: In embryonic mouse neocortex, BPs down-regulate the endogenous expression of ECM components in comparison with aRG, in line with the lower proliferative capacity of the former than the latter.
source: Specifically, in embryonic mouse neocortex, BPs down-regulate the endogenous expression of ECM components in comparison with aRG, in line with the lower proliferative capacity of the former than the latter (Arai et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Arai et al., 2011).

claim: The expression of ECM components is down-regulated in the embryonic mouse SVZ compared to the VZ, whereas in fetal human neocortex this expression is maintained not only in the VZ, but also inner SVZ (ISVZ) and outer SVZ (OSVZ).
source: Consistent with this, the expression of ECM components is down-regulated in the embryonic mouse SVZ compared to the VZ, whereas in fetal human neocortex this expression is maintained not only in the VZ, but also inner SVZ (ISVZ) and outer SVZ (OSVZ) (Fietz et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Fietz et al., 2012).

claim: Not only human aRG, but also human bRG show a characteristic expression of ECM components.
source: Accordingly, not only human aRG, but also human bRG show a characteristic expression of ECM components (Florio et al., 2015; Pollen et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is based on previous studies cited in the text (Florio et al., 2015; Pollen et al., 2015).

claim: The targeted activation of integrins, specifically integrin αvβ3, on mouse BPs promotes their proliferation.
source: Moreover, when mimicking the physiological situation in the fetal human SVZ in an embryonic mouse model, the targeted activation of integrins, the canonical receptors for ECM components, specifically of integrin αvβ3, on mouse BPs promotes their proliferation (Stenzel et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Stenzel et al., 2014).

claim: Inhibition of integrin αvβ3 in an ex vivo model of the developing neocortex of the ferret reduces the BP pool size, in particular that of bRG.
source: Conversely, inhibition of integrin αvβ3 in an ex vivo model of the developing neocortex of the ferret, which exhibits an expanded, folded cerebral cortex, reduces the BP pool size, in particular that of bRG (Fietz et al., 2010)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Fietz et al., 2010).

claim: BPs in species with an expanded neocortex, such as human and ferret, exhibit an increased number of cell processes used to receive extrinsic pro-proliferative signals via integrin signaling, notably involving integrin β1.
source: Furthermore, we have recently shown that BPs in species with an expanded neocortex, such as human and ferret, exhibit an increased number of cell processes; these are used to receive extrinsic pro-proliferative signals via integrin signaling, notably involving integrin β1 (Kalebic et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study by the authors cited in the text (Kalebic et al., 2019).

claim: Blocking of integrin β1 in fetal human neocortex results in a reduction of BP proliferation.
source: Blocking of integrin β1 in fetal human neocortex thus resulted in a reduction of BP proliferation (Kalebic et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study by the authors cited in the text (Kalebic et al., 2019).

claim: An increased expression of ECM components by BPs contributes to generate a proliferative niche away from the ventricular surface and to promote BP proliferation via increased integrin signaling.
source: Taken together, these findings have led to the general concept that an increased expression of ECM components by BPs contributes to generate a proliferative niche away from the ventricular surface and to promote BP proliferation via increased integrin signaling (Fietz et al., 2010; Fietz et al., 2012; Kalebic et al., 2019; Long and Huttner, 2019; Stenzel et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is a general concept based on multiple previous studies cited in the text.

claim: An in silico analysis of transcription factors expressed in embryonic mouse vs. fetal human germinal zones and predicted to bind to promoters of ECM genes has revealed Sox9 as a promising candidate to drive expression of ECM components in the human SVZ.
source: An in silico analysis of transcription factors expressed in embryonic mouse vs. fetal human germinal zones and predicted to bind to promoters of ECM genes has revealed Sox9 as a promising candidate to drive expression of ECM components in the human SVZ (Fietz et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study cited in the text (Fietz et al., 2012).

claim: Sox9 is involved in driving glia-specific gene expression.
source: In this context, given the role of Sox9 in driving glia-specific gene expression (Huang et al., 2015; Kang et al., 2012; Klum et al., 2018; Martini et al., 2013; Molofsky et al., 2013; Nagao et al., 2016; Selvaraj et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is based on multiple previous studies cited in the text.

claim: Sox9 is involved in the neurogenesis-to-gliogenesis switch in the developing spinal cord.
source: and in the neurogenesis-to-gliogenesis switch in the developing spinal cord (Finzsch et al., 2008; Molofsky et al., 2013; Stolt et al., 2003; Stolt and Wegner, 2010; Wegner and Stolt, 2005)
evidence: The claim is based on multiple previous studies cited in the text.

claim: In the developing mouse neocortex, neurogenesis and gliogenesis take place sequentially, that is, after neurogenesis, SVZ progenitors of oligodendrocytes and astrocytes are being generated.
source: In the developing mouse neocortex, neurogenesis and gliogenesis take place sequentially, that is, after neurogenesis, SVZ progenitors of oligodendrocytes and astrocytes are being generated (Kriegstein and Alvarez-Buylla, 2009; Merkle et al., 2004)
evidence: The claim is based on previous studies cited in the text (Kriegstein and Alvarez-Buylla, 2009; Merkle et al., 2004).

claim: In the SVZ of gyrencephalic species, such as human, macaque and ferret, neurogenic and gliogenic progenitors co-exist at later stages of neurogenesis.
source: In contrast, in the SVZ of gyrencephalic species, such as human, macaque and ferret, neurogenic and gliogenic progenitors co-exist at later stages of neurogenesis (Martínez-Cerdeño et al., 2012; Rash et al., 2019; Reillo and Borrell, 2012; Reillo et al., 2011; Zecevic et al., 2005)
evidence: The claim is based on previous studies cited in the text (Martínez-Cerdeño et al., 2012; Rash et al., 2019; Reillo and Borrell, 2012; Reillo et al., 2011; Zecevic et al., 2005).
